meaning: A fake emergency call or message in which a crook pretends to be a grandchild who needs help.
clues: A stranger lies about who they are and pushes you to act fast.
The person contacting you claims to be someone else.
The caller says a grandchild is in trouble and needs quick help.
The safest move is to pause and check with your family using a number you know.
Its name starts with G and includes a word for a parent's parent.
assumes: A government impersonation scam pretends to be a government worker
A utility scam uses a false power or water warning
A charity scam asks for money while pretending to help a cause

decoys.meaning: A trick where someone pretends to be a government worker.
A trick that threatens to shut off power or water unless you pay.
A trick that asks for donations while pretending to help a cause.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Try it with someone you trust. If a caller says a relative needs help, hang up and call that relative using a number you know.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: When a family story sounded urgent, we checked with another relative. A second call can clear up a lot.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Do not send money or give private details while you feel rushed. Take a breath and check the story.

blank.sentence: A caller said, 'Grandma, I am in trouble, send help now.' That was a ___.

why: Crooks use a family emergency to rush you, so pause and call your family.

situations.text: A caller says your grandchild is in trouble. You hang up and call your grandchild on a number you know.
situations.why: A second call can clear up a lot.
